# Required Packages

```{r}
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(dplyr)
library(skimr)
library(lme4)
library(openxlsx)
```

# Raw Data

```{r}
Raw_Data <- read_excel("raw_data/BIOL3208 Results.xlsx")
```

# Raw Data Sanity Checks

```{r}
skim(Raw_Data)
```

```
The Mean_Value, ROI_Area_pixel and ROI_Area_M2 are all characters, we want these as numeric for analysis. This can be achieved using:
```

```{r}
Raw_Data$Mean_Value <- factor(Raw_Data$Mean_Value)
Raw_Data$Mean_Value <- as.numeric(levels(Raw_Data$Mean_Value)[Raw_Data$Mean_Value])
```

```{r}
Raw_Data$ROI_Area_pixel <- factor(Raw_Data$ROI_Area_pixel)
Raw_Data$ROI_Area_pixel <- as.numeric(levels(Raw_Data$ROI_Area_pixel)[Raw_Data$ROI_Area_pixel])
```

```{r}
Raw_Data$ROI_Area_M2 <- factor(Raw_Data$ROI_Area_M2)
Raw_Data$ROI_Area_M2 <- as.numeric(levels(Raw_Data$ROI_Area_M2)[Raw_Data$ROI_Area_M2])
```

```
We would also expect there to be 36 (2 treatments x 2 times x 3 genotypes x 3 weeks) combinations in these columns, lets check that
```

```{r}
Raw_Data |> 
  distinct(Date_Measured, Time_Measured, Strain, Treatment)
```

```
29 are observed instead of 36 (this is due to several combinations not being assessed, such as Week 3 afternoon sets, due to time constraints)
```

```{r}
Filtered_Data <- Raw_Data[Retained_Stomata,]
```

```
This next bit is unique to my work, I had to export the filtered data containing my measurements of stomatal aperture (since I only measured the aperture of filtered stomata to save time, whereas for general fluorescence I measured all stomata and then blind filtered the stomata for inclusion/exclusion). I would really recommend not being an idiot like me, just filter the stomata AT THE START and then do fluorescence + stomata, I wasted a lot of time doing it this way...
```

```{r}
Filtered_Data <- read_excel("Filtered_Data.xlsx")
Filtered_Data <- Filtered_Data[-(1:10),]
```


# Calculating Fluorescence Scaled to Area

```
We are interested in the fluorescence value scaled according to the stomatal area, so we need to turn the area measurements to kpixel & uM^2, and then divide the fluorescence row by these new area measurements to obtain fluorescence scaled by area for each stomata.
```

```{r}
Filtered_Data$ROI_Area_pixel <- Filtered_Data$ROI_Area_pixel/1000
Filtered_Data$ROI_Area_M2 <- Filtered_Data$ROI_Area_M2 * 10^12
```

```{r}
Filtered_Data$Area_Scale_Fluorescence <- Filtered_Data$Mean_Value/Filtered_Data$ROI_Area_M2
```

```{r}
Filtered_Data[rowSums(is.na(Filtered_Data)) > 0,]
```

# Filtered Data Sanity Checks

```{r}
skim(Filtered_Data)
```

```

table(Filtered_Data$Treatment)
```

# Checking the number of entries for each combination

```
This will be really useful later on for when adding n = to each of your graph columns
```


```{r}
Stomata_Per_Combination <- Filtered_Data |> 
  group_by(Date_Measured, Time_Measured, Strain, Treatment) |> 
  summarize(Count = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

# Plotting the area scaled fluorescence for each combination of Date, Time, Genotype and Treatment

```
This is useful for comparison, when filtering the data according to genotype and time_measured down below you can compare the graph results with this simple output to make sure nothing has gone wrong with filtering.
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = Filtered_Data, aes(x = Treatment, y = Area_Scale_Fluorescence)) +
  geom_boxplot() + 
  facet_grid(Strain ~ Date_Measured + Time_Measured)
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = Filtered_Data, aes(x = Treatment, y = Width_Stomatal_Aperture)) +
  geom_boxplot() + 
  facet_grid(Strain ~ Date_Measured + Time_Measured)
```


```
We can look at WT specifically, separating based on morning and afternoon (given the differences which appear visually comparing these groupings). We can then repeat this for each strain.
```

```{r}
WT_Data_AM <- Filtered_Data |> 
  filter(Strain == "WT" & Time_Measured == "AM")
```

```{r}
WT_Plot_AM <- ggplot(data = WT_Data_AM, aes(x = interaction(Treatment, Date_Measured), y = Area_Scale_Fluorescence,  fill = Date_Measured)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = "red") +
  geom_jitter(aes(y = Area_Scale_Fluorescence), width = 0.2, size = 0.5) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = F) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Fluorescence scaled to Area (Arbitrary/uM2)") +
  ylim(0,10) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = 9.7, label = "**") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 1, xend = 2, y = 9.5, yend = 9.5)) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = 9.05, label = "1.83x") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 1, xend = 2, y = 8.75, yend = 8.75), arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "cm"), type = "closed"), size = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 3.5, y = 9.7, label = "*") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 3, xend = 4, y = 9.5, yend = 9.5)) +
  annotate("text", x = 3.5, y = 9.05, label = "1.37x") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 3, xend = 4, y = 8.75, yend = 8.75), arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "cm"), type = "closed"), size = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 5.5, y = 9.8, label = "n.s") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 5, xend = 6, y = 9.5, yend = 9.5)) +
  annotate("text", x = 5.5, y = 9.05, label = "0.77x") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 5, xend = 6, y = 8.75, yend = 8.75), arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "cm"), type = "closed"), size = 0.5)

ggsave("WT_Plot_AM.png", plot = WT_Plot_AM, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 600)
```

# Planning Comparisons

## The end goal will be comparing the effect of treatment and strain on the fluorescence value when scaled by area, so we can compare if there are differences between strains for the treatments. 

## However, we also want to test if across the strains there is a difference between the weeks (refering generally to growth stage). We will also need to test if there is a difference between the morning (90 minute light) and afternoon (360 minute light) sets, if they don't we can group them for increased replicates.

## Testing the Effect of Treatment Time (Morning vs Afternoon)

## ANOVA Assumptions

```{r}
#1) The two independent variables, the factors should consist of two or more categorical and independent levels. 
#2) The dependent variable, the measurement should be continuous and approximately normally distributed within each group. 
  # Probably assumed due to large sample size
#3) The observations should be independent. Sample from an entire population. 
  # Stomata are considered independent due to how unique they are from each other
#4) The variance within each group should be approximately the same (homogeneity of variance, homoscedaticity). 
#5) Residuals should be normally distributed. 
  #qqnorm(X$residuals)
  #qqline(X$residuals)
#6) The design should be balanced, with the same number of observations in each category. 
#7) There should be no significant outliers. 
#8) The measurements in every group represent a random sample from a population. 

```

# Standard parametric ANOVA

```{r}
total_aov <- aov(Area_Scale_Fluorescence ~ Strain * Treatment * Date_Measured * Time_Measured, data = Filtered_Data)

par(mfrow = c(1,2))
hist(total_aov$residuals)
qqnorm(total_aov$residuals)
qqline(total_aov$residuals)
par(mfrow = c(1,1))

summary(total_aov)
```

```{r}
TukeyHSD(total_aov)
```



# Statistically Assessing Residual Normality

```{r}
ggplot(data = Filtered_Data, aes(x = Area_Scale_Fluorescence)) +
  geom_histogram()
```


```{r}
shapiro.test(Filtered_Data$Area_Scale_Fluorescence)
```


```{r}
shapiro.test(total_aov$residuals)
```

```
This suggests the data is not normally distributed? But I also know statistical tests will reject normality with large sample sizes, when deviations might not be extreme enough to use alternatives?
```

```{r}
leveneTest(Area_Scale_Fluorescence ~ Strain * Treatment * Date_Measured * Time_Measured, data = Filtered_Data)
```
